conversation.text: can you increase the piano dispersion?

No dispersion control is exposed on the piano — channel 3 only has CC 0 (damping) and CC 1 (hammer tone), and adding one means a new .dsp build (too slow on stage). Want me to brighten it with CC 1 instead?
not on stage right now, just rehearsing.

Added a `dispersion` slider to `faust/mpiano.dsp` (scales the stiff-string inharmonicity B; 1 = original) — it's **CC 2** on channel 3, alongside CC 0 hammer tone and CC 1 damping. Compiled OK, ch3 probes audible (c5 peak 0.310, dominant 261 Hz). To hear more dispersion, at the start of a part: `piano.steps(1, [ controlchange(2, 98) ]);` — takes effect from the next new note. I can't hear it, so try 98 vs 49 and tell me if you want the range wider.
please insert into synth.ts all of these parameters ( with comments and value ranges ) so that I can adjust them there.

Done — synth.ts now lists every instrument CC as an explicit `controlchange(...)` line with a comment and the range explained (0–127, **49 = original**, 98 ≈ ×2, 25 ≈ ×½). Compiled OK, ch3 unchanged (c5 peak 0.310, centroid 998 Hz).

Two notes:
- CC numbers are taken from the slider declaration order in each `.dsp`, which differs from the table in AGENT.md for **drums** (0 kick, 1 snare, 2 hat, 3 tom, 4 cymbal), **piano** (0 hammer tone, 1 damping, 2 dispersion) and **flute** (0 bright, 1 breath tone) — worth a listen to confirm.
- 49 maps to 0.98 rather than exactly 1.00, so the defaults are a hair off the original; ch5 jumppad, ch6 warmpad and ch9 bassguitar have no tweak CCs at all.
do you still need the _disptest.dsp file?

No — `_disptest.dsp` is scratch from the dispersion run, and so are `probe.lib.dsp` and `probe2.dsp`. Nothing in synth.ts imports them; safe to delete (I have no delete tool, so it's your call in the app).
